common_name: LeCompte Chaste Tree (Louisiana Select Purple-Flowered Vitex)

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container-grown specimens in well-drained soil in full sun; LeCompte was selected in Louisiana for exceptionally long, dense flower spikes and strong repeat bloom through the Gulf South growing season.

directions: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or set out container-grown plants in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun. LeCompte is a Louisiana-origin chaste tree selection prized for producing some of the longest, most densely packed lavender-purple flower spikes of any named vitex, opening in flushes from late spring through fall on new wood. The aromatic, gray-green palmately compound foliage adds a light sage scent when brushed, and the plant shrugs off summer heat, drought, and poor soil once established. Cut the whole plant back hard to 12-18 inches in late winter each year to keep growth vigorous, maintain a manageable size, and maximize the following season's flower spike count. Bees and butterflies work the long bloom spikes heavily all summer.

common_name: Silver Spire Chaste Tree (White-Flowered Vitex Selection)

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container-grown specimens in well-drained soil in full sun; Silver Spire is the standard pure-white-flowered chaste tree selection, offering the same toughness as blue-flowered vitex with clean white flower spikes for a lighter garden palette.

directions: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container specimens in well-drained, average to poor soil in full sun. Silver Spire is the most widely available white-flowered chaste tree cultivar, producing slender spikes of pure white flowers rather than the lavender-blue typical of the species, making it a useful choice for moon gardens, white borders, or breaking up a planting dominated by blue and purple vitex selections. It blooms repeatedly on new growth from late spring into fall, tolerates heat, drought, and lean soil as well as any blue-flowered selection, and carries the same aromatic, gray-green palmate foliage. Prune hard to 12-18 inches above ground in late winter to renew growth and encourage the heaviest flower production the following season.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
